chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Al-Hasan ibn Atiyya, from Ismail ibn Jabir, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
The one who combs his beard seventy times, and enumerates it one by one, the Satan would not come near him for forty days.

key_terms.سَرَّحَ: To comb or groom (specifically the beard)

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual benefit of combing the beard seventy times according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In the Shia tradition, grooming is viewed not merely as hygiene but as an act of worship that reflects inner purity; this specific practice of combing the beard seventy times with mindful enumeration is believed to create a spiritual shield against Satan for forty days. This highlights the concept of *tathir* (purification) where physical care serves as a vessel for spiritual vigilance, a theme emphasized by Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) in his teachings on the etiquette of the body.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Al Hassan Bin Atiyya, from Ismail Bin Jabir, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘The one who combs his beard seventy times, and enumerates it one by one, the Satan<sup>la</sup> would not come near him for forty days’.
en.sarwar: 10. A number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad from al-Hassan ibn ‘Atiyyah from ’Isma‘il ibn Jabir who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
If one uses his comb seventy times and counts it one by one, Satan will not come close to him for forty days.’”
